sampling.order: Seeded random order within every case/fork block; verification separate; all measured observations retained

results.title: Worker scaling · 1 process

task.arithmetic: Ordered IEEE-754 f64; independent stateless source instances
task.ordering: 196608 accepted turns partitioned evenly among independent workers; no shared mutable state; every worker endpoint verified

measurement.setup: Executable built before timing; binary, dependencies and compiler revision pinned
measurement.reset: Fresh process for every independent fork
measurement.destruction: Complete shutdown and owned output release included
measurement.cache: OS caches uncontrolled; independent process forks
measurement.threads: One application thread per worker process; supervisor uses one waiting thread per process; source-catalog setup may start its short-lived builder thread
measurement.partition: Strong scaling: fixed total turns; contiguous equal partitions; no other timed campaigns overlap
measurement.comparison_note: Same inputs, accepted turns, warmup and output/retention obligations, paired on the same machine. Rust is an independent AOT task implementation with typed input validation, change detection and owned publication. Rust uses native ownership; Mech additionally performs its runtime admission, dependency scheduling, budget accounting and turn summary. This measures the cost of completing the task through each path, not a language-wide speed claim. Compilation is outside the resident timer. Rust preparation is not presented as a Mech artifact or JIT metric. Complete supervised group startup through exit, fixed total work; one execution thread per process.
